valuation_philosophy.methodology: Residual Income (Excess-Return) Model on Tangible Book Value, discounted at Cost of Equity — NOT a standard unlevered FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.rationale: SRBK is a bank holding company. 'Free cash flow' is not a meaningful concept for a depository institution because loan and deposit flows swamp any FCF proxy and capital is regulated (not freely distributable). The correct framework for a bank is a residual-income / excess-return model: intrinsic equity value = current tangible book value (TBV) + PV of future residual income (where residual income = (ROE - Cost of Equity) x beginning tangible book value) + PV of a terminal exit value based on an assumed exit Price/Tangible-Book-Value multiple (in lieu of a Gordon-growth terminal value on FCF). This directly captures the core economic reality here: SRBK's ROE (~2-5% across scenarios) is persistently below its ~9.5-10.5% cost of equity, so the bank is a going-concern value destroyer at the margin — the offsetting value drivers are (a) sub-tangible-book buybacks that are mechanically accretive to continuing shareholders, (b) NIM/ROE recovery as excess post-IPO capital gets deployed, and (c) M&A optionality once the September 2026 post-conversion moratorium expires, which could crystallize value via a takeout at a P/TBV premium.
valuation_philosophy.wacc_field_note: The 'wacc' field in the assumptions block below is actually COST OF EQUITY (CoE), not a blended WACC. Deposits/borrowings are not treated as DCF-style debt financing a project; they are the bank's raw material, already reflected in net interest income. Using CoE (not WACC) to discount equity-level residual income is the standard bank-valuation convention.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value_note: Terminal value in the 'terminal_growth' sensitivity axis is replaced by an EXIT PRICE/TANGIBLE-BOOK-VALUE MULTIPLE applied to projected terminal tangible book value, rather than a Gordon-growth perpetuity on FCF. This is standard practice for bank/thrift takeout and going-concern valuation. Sensitivity table rows/columns therefore vary Cost of Equity and Exit P/TBV instead of WACC and terminal growth.

inputs.notes: Goodwill of $20.417M is fixed (from Regal Bancorp merger, Sept 2023, confirmed in FY2025 10-K). Core deposit intangible was $6.291M at 6/30/25, amortizing per 10-K schedule ($1.167M FY2026, $0.951M FY2027, $0.774M FY2028, $0.657M FY2029, $2.742M thereafter); CDI estimated at $5.416M as of 3/31/26 (3/4 of FY2026 amortization applied). Book value of $184.5M / 8.2M shares = $22.50/share (BVPS) vs $19.35/share tangible (TBVPS) — the valuation anchor for a bank.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Standard CAGR growth-rate selection logic does not apply to SRBK. Revenue CAGR (~50% 3yr) and Equity CAGR (~18% 3yr) are both severely DISTORTED and NOT usable as organic growth proxies: (1) Revenue/NII jumped mechanically due to the Sept-2023 Regal Bancorp acquisition roughly doubling the balance sheet, not organic growth; FY2024 also had a net LOSS (-$1.59 EPS) from merger-related CECL day-1 provisioning and one-time expenses, making EPS CAGR mathematically meaningless (negative-to-positive base). (2) Equity CAGR is inflated by the Sept-2023 IPO capital raise (~$75M+ of fresh equity), not retained-earnings growth. The cleanest organic metric is Net Interest Income growth on a post-merger, apples-to-apples basis: NII grew only +0.68% FY2024->FY2025, consistent with a bank still working through excess capital deployment and NIM pressure rather than a growth story. This is why the DCF model below uses a residual-income/ROE framework anchored to tangible book value rather than any of these distorted growth CAGRs.

base.rationale: Gradual NIM/ROE recovery from ~3.0% NIM currently toward ~3.4-3.6% as excess IPO capital is deployed into higher-yielding multi-family/CRE/C&I loans; continued ~3%/yr share count shrink via buybacks (in line with the active 10%-of-shares authorization) plus a modest, growing dividend (20% payout, consistent with the June 2026 hike to $0.06/qtr); exit at ~1.0x TBV (i.e., slightly below, reflecting still-subpar ROE) assuming no M&A transaction occurs and the bank continues as a going concern, valued at roughly par to tangible book.

bull.rationale: Acquisition scenario: the standard 3-year post-conversion anti-takeover moratorium expires September 2026, opening the door to a sale. Faster ROE improvement (mix-shift into CRE/multifamily/C&I accelerates, NIM expands faster) makes SRBK a more attractive target; overcapitalized, well-run, recently-converted NJ thrifts of this size typically get acquired at 1.15x-1.30x tangible book (midpoint 1.25x modeled here) within 2-3 years of moratorium expiration. Modeled as a 3-year exit (not 5) to reflect the earlier expected transaction timing, discounted at a slightly lower CoE (9.5%) reflecting reduced illiquidity/uncertainty once a deal is signed.

bear.rationale: No sale materializes; ROE stays stuck in the low-2% to high-2% range as sub-scale cost structure, deposit-cost competition, and slow capital deployment persist. Buybacks continue but decelerate (regulatory approval needed above 10% of net worth/12mo, and management may conserve capital if earnings stay weak) providing only partial offset to persistent value destruction (ROE well below CoE). Exit at a discount to tangible book (0.775x) consistent with chronically sub-peer profitability and no strategic catalyst; slightly higher CoE (10.5%) reflects elevated uncertainty/illiquidity risk in this scenario.

base.note: Entry price for a 15% annualized CAGR to the base-case Y5 terminal (exit) value of $21.80/share, which itself embeds only a ~0.95x exit P/TBV on ~$22.95 ending TBVPS — i.e., even the terminal value assumes SRBK is still valued near/below tangible book in 5 years given persistently sub-CoE ROE.

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows = Cost of Equity (CoE), Columns = Exit Price/Tangible-Book-Value multiple (in place of terminal growth rate for a bank residual-income model). Matrix computed on BASE case ROE/buyback/dividend path over 5 years.

probability_weighted.note: Bull (M&A takeout) weighted at 30% reflecting the plausible-but-unconfirmed nature of a sale — the 3-year post-conversion moratorium expires September 2026 and small NJ thrifts are frequent consolidation targets, but no deal has been announced as of July 2026; only buybacks and a 20% dividend increase have occurred to date. Base (45%) and Bear (25%) together capture the more likely going-concern organic-improvement path, where SRBK's ROE recovers only gradually and remains below its cost of equity throughout the projection window.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied P/B 0.66x is below the 1.33x threshold (1.5x historical max 0.89x); implied P/E 23.7x is below 2.0x the historical average; base-case upside is negative (-26.4%), so the price-in-upper-half-of-range condition is moot.
sanity_check.methodology_note: Residual-income model on tangible book at cost of equity was used from the outset (FCF DCF is invalid for a bank), which structurally prevents the peak-FCF extrapolation failure mode this check targets. EV/EBITDA checks skipped as not meaningful for depository institutions.
